what: Each time the cursor moves more than 4px over the photo, a brush-stroke ring (60px, size .2 · opacity .5) is stamped at that spot. Every frame it rotates .02 rad, grows by .09 and fades by a factor of .96 (max 90 marks). The marks are drawn onto an offscreen buffer with additive blending, and their red value r is used to rotate the photo by θ = Pushes by r × .1 in the r·2π direction so a swirl ripple spreads (WebGL). Drawing stops once the cursor leaves and all trails have faded · video and continuously drawing canvases are twisted the same way (live), and stamp size, opacity and growth decay are accepted as options (Brand stamps a plate .65× the board height at .3×, grows it by .94×+.07 and erases it quickly by ×.84)

options.size: Mark size (px), default 60 — write it like ”0.65h” for a ratio of panel height
options.gap: Minimum movement (px) to register a new mark, default 4 — a panel-height ratio like ”0.0065h” also works
options.[data-fx-part=image]: Warped photo — img·canvas·video (autoplay·loop are up to the user), or a placeholder with data-label (painted with the skin color panel). The canvas is laid over that cell (over the parent if it is img·canvas·video).
options.decay: Scale-up damping — Multiplier = decay × multiplier + grow, default 1 (plain addition)
options.live: If 1, the panel is a constantly changing canvas, so it is re-read every frame while on screen (video does this by itself)

use: …

note: Runs on mouse only (touch shows the photo as is). The brush stroke graphic is a ring drawn on the fly, so its feel differs slightly from the original brush artwork. Even if a cover text (a description panel that appears on hover) sits over the photo, the cursor over the whole element is tracked, so drawing continues.
